_meta: Top 100+ most phished brands. Source: APWG, OpenPhish reports 2024-2026

not_in_model._why: Names the served ML model (data/model_meta.json, features_version 6) was not trained with. url_features._max_brand_similarity leaves them out, so a new brand does not move that feature for every host resembling it; is_typosquat and brand_in_subdomain do fire on its look-alikes, as they mean to. Empty this list when the model is retrained.

measured._about: Global brands added with a measured false-positive pass, one entry per owner, in data/typosquat_targets_ru.json's format (api/services/ru_brands.py parses each entry; api/services/scoring.py _load_measured_global_groups). Their names are also in 'brands'. They are compared under the slip rule (scoring._rule_for): under 8 letters one substitution has to be a slip of the hand. Every domain was checked on 2026-10-05 — name servers, where http:// lands, the page title, whois where DNS alone was not proof. The pass and every hit it found: docs/benchmarks/2026-10-05-global-brands.md.
measured._selection: A brand is here when the PhishTank and TweetFeed week sampled in docs/benchmarks/2026-10-04-ml-eval.json has hosts imitating it AND its false positives on the Tranco top-1M (with and without subdomains), the macOS dictionary as <word>.com and the Russian legit sets are explained below. Considered and left out (same document): tmobile ('t' + the word mobile: 335 mobile.de hosts), sharepoint (share/point compounds: chargepoint.com), aruba (a country; ariba.com), interbank (inter + a word: 18 top-1M neighbours), raiffeisen (a cooperative movement's name, hundreds of independent banks), caixa (Portuguese 'box'; caixa.cv), sunrise and kleinanzeigen (ordinary words), inpost and verizon (no host in the week; inpost has 9 other owners one edit away).

alternates._about: Registrable domains the owners of names in 'brands' run besides the listed one (googlemail.com, yahoo.de), and other owners' sites the rule reads as a listed name (hicloud.com is Huawei's, not iCloud's). Until 2026-10-23 the Tranco top-100k allowlist answered for them before the typosquat rule ran; the licensed ranking (Majestic Million + Chrome UX Report, PR #284) does not carry them. One entry per owner, parsed by api/services/ru_brands.py parse_alternates: 'names' are the names in 'brands' the entry is about, 'official' the owner's own domains, 'unrelated' other owners' same-shaped sites, each with its dated evidence. Exact registrable-domain exemptions (scoring._BRAND_LEGIT_DOMAINS, as in the Russian file) and nothing else: the names keep their rule, which is what 'measured' changes.
alternates._evidence: A domain is listed only when BOTH hold: (1) it is the owner's — its registrant (RDAP or the registry's WHOIS) is the owner, or its registrar is a brand-protection registrar (MarkMonitor, CSC, Com Laude, SafeNames, Lexsynergy, Abion, GoDaddy Corporate Domains, Meta's RegistrarSafe / RegistrarSEC), or the TLD is the owner's own (.google, .globo, .bmw); where the registry publishes no registrant for any holder (.de, .ru), the name servers must sit in the owner's netblock and serve its main domain; (2) the owner runs it now — its name servers are the owner's own or the set its main domain is delegated to, or a TLS certificate names the owner (OV/EV), or one certificate covers it with the owner's main sites, or Certificate Transparency logs show certificates for its names from the owner's own CA. A redirect to the brand is not evidence. Privacy-proxied, recently registered or cheap-hosted domains are not listed, nor zones where anyone can get a name of their own (trycloudflare.com, github.dev, azure.net, onmicrosoft.com, and cloud.ru, whose S3 storage serves customers' buckets at <bucket>.s3.cloud.ru): an exemption covers every host under the registrable. The 2026-10-23 review of all 190 names the rule flagged among the 44,736 that left the allowlist, with the ones left out and why, is in the pull request that added this section (fix/brand-alternates).
